# Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler?

On 29 October 2026, Anthropic's published crawler guide describes separate robots for training collection, search and user-directed retrieval, with robots.txt controls for each. Choose the control that matches your purpose. In our construction capture dated 22 September 2026, Claude named Buildertrend in 21 of 30 valid answers.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Reported.** [Anthropic's crawler guide](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler), read on 29 October 2026, distinguishes ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User. It describes ClaudeBot as collecting material that could contribute to training, Claude-SearchBot as supporting search, and Claude-User as retrieving content at a user's direction. The guide gives robots.txt instructions for controlling each robot on the relevant site or subdomain.

**Measured.** Buildertrend's 21 naming appearances come from the Claude cells in the [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695): ten construction buyer questions, three runs per question, 30 retained Claude answers. Other engines have their own cells and are outside this figure.

The answer count does not measure the effect of blocking any of Anthropic's robots.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Claude answered the general contractor (GC) question “best construction software for a small GC that needs estimating and scheduling without Procore complexity” on 22 September 2026, run 1, with the fragment “Projul, JobTread, and Buildertrend”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Pick the purpose first. If your decision concerns future training collection, read the ClaudeBot rule rather than treating Claude-SearchBot as another spelling of it. Anthropic gives the robots different jobs, so a single company-level instruction such as “block Claude” leaves the intended access unclear.

If you want company information available to user-directed retrieval, inspect the Claude-User instruction separately. The Buildertrend count describes answers observed in September; it is not a record of whether Claude-User requested Buildertrend's pages. Keep the access setting and the answer observation as separate items in your notes.

For server load, Anthropic also documents Crawl-delay separately from its full-site disallow example. Read the exact option before choosing between slowing a robot and excluding it. Apply the decision to the subdomain whose content you mean, as the published guide instructs.

# How does Claude web search work?

Claude web search retrieves material from the web to inform an answer and supplies citations when that search capability is used, according to Anthropic's guide read on 29 October 2026. Read the citation beside the particular claim. Our 22 September 2026 construction panel recorded Procore in 21 of 30 Claude answers.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Reported.** [Anthropic's web-search guide](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/10684626-enabling-and-using-web-search), read on 29 October 2026, describes Claude invoking a search tool for relevant current information, processing sources and returning direct citations. It also describes web fetch for retrieving a supplied page when web search is enabled. The guide describes workspace and member controls, and separately notes that the new Claude experience has no web-search toggle: it searches when helpful.

**Measured.** The [September release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) records Procore's 21 naming appearances within Claude's 30 valid construction answers. The ten buyer questions and three repeats define that base. This figure counts the checked product name, not citations to Procore's own domain.

Those naming cells cannot establish which source Claude used for a claim or how it weighted that source.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Claude answered the general contractor (GC) question “best construction software for a small GC that needs estimating and scheduling without Procore complexity” on 22 September 2026, run 2, with the fragment “a way to track costs against budget in real time”. The Key Takeaway describes a contractor's workflow need; this historical wording is not an independently verified feature of one product.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** In a managed Claude workspace, read the current-experience note as well as Anthropic's workspace instructions. The guide documents an organization-level permission and member control, but explicitly says the new Claude experience has no web-search toggle. If that is your interface, the missing toggle is consistent with the documented experience. Keep the experience and date with the saved answer.

If you supplied a direct URL, distinguish the web-fetch case described in the guide from asking Claude to discover sources. Reading a selected Procore page answers a different source question from finding independent pages for a construction comparison. Keep the selected address with that observation.

The construction question makes a visible difference in this Claude sample. Procore was named in zero of three answers for a small residential builder, and in all three for a mid-sized general contractor. Keep those exact buyer contexts with the citations you inspect, rather than using the pooled 21 as the answer to both questions.

# Which construction software does Claude recommend?

Buildertrend and Procore each appeared in 21 of 30 Claude construction-software answers captured on 22 September 2026. Their equal totals hide a useful distinction: the small-residential-builder question named Buildertrend in all three answers and Procore in none. The mid-sized-general-contractor question reversed those two counts. Read that buyer context before treating the shared total as a recommendation for your firm.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** In the [September construction release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), Claude answered ten fixed questions three times each. The 30 valid answers cover residential building, general contracting, subcontractors, capital projects and comparisons. All were captured on 22 September 2026; the release was published the next day.

Buildertrend's 21 matches correspond to 70.0 percent. A descriptive 95 percent Wilson uncertainty range runs from 52.1 to 83.3 percent. Generalizing that range to all construction buyers would go beyond this fixed panel.

| --- | --- |
| Autodesk Construction Cloud | 9 of 30 |
| Buildertrend | 21 of 30 |
| Buildxact | 7 of 30 |

Claude named sixteen of the 22 checked vendors somewhere in this set. An appearance is a match under the release's vendor-name rules, rather than a scored endorsement. The table preserves the six checked names with no match and lists every vendor alphabetically.

The residential and general-contractor cells are parts of the same 30-answer total. They show where two equal totals came from; they do not reveal why Claude selected a name. The records also do not test implementation quality or confirm that a cited page caused the selection.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Claude responded to “best construction management software for a small residential builder” on 22 September 2026, run 3, and described Buildertrend with the fragment “project scheduling, job costing, document management, subcontractor coordination”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Locate your contracting context before assembling a product list. A residential builder's question, an owner's capital-project comparison and a subcontractor's question should remain separate records. Pooling them can conceal the very distinction you need to judge an answer.

For each candidate, identify the claim you would rely on in a buying discussion. If the answer describes estimating, scheduling or a project connection, ask for dated product evidence for that specific claim. A recorded appearance of Buildertrend or Procore does not establish the detail by itself.

If you publish construction-product information, explain the supported work and its boundary on the relevant page. Keep missing facts separate from a missing brand name. The first can be checked against a source; the second needs the actual question and captured answer before you can investigate it.

# Which dental software does Claude recommend?

26 of 30 Claude dental-software answers named Dentrix in our [22 September 2026 collection](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695); Curve Dental appeared in 25 and Open Dental in 24. These are naming observations rather than votes from dental practices. Dentrix, Dentrix Ascend and Dentrix Enterprise remain separate rows in the source, so a count for one cannot establish a claim about another edition.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [September dental Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) supplies ten fixed questions with three Claude answers apiece. All 30 Claude answers were usable. They cover new practices, very small offices, alternatives, comparisons and a dental service organization with multiple locations. Captures took place on 22 September 2026, before the release on 23 September.

The 26 Dentrix appearances give a rate of 86.7 percent and a descriptive 95 percent Wilson uncertainty range of 70.3 to 94.7 percent. Those figures concern recorded answers, without measuring how many dental practices would select the product.

| Checked vendor | Named in valid Claude answers |
| --- | --- |
| ABELDent | 1 of 30 |
| ACE Dental | 0 of 30 |
| Adit | 3 of 30 |
| CareStack | 11 of 30 |
| Carestream Dental | 1 of 30 |
| Curve Dental | 25 of 30 |
| Dentally | 0 of 30 |
| DentiMax | 6 of 30 |
| Dentrix | 26 of 30 |
| Dentrix Ascend | 22 of 30 |
| Dentrix Enterprise | 5 of 30 |
| DSN | 0 of 30 |
| Eaglesoft | 18 of 30 |
| MacPractice | 0 of 30 |
| Open Dental | 24 of 30 |
| Oryx Dental | 4 of 30 |
| Planet DDS (Denticon) | 12 of 30 |
| Practice-Web | 3 of 30 |
| tab32 | 14 of 30 |
| XLDent | 0 of 30 |

Fifteen of twenty checked dental vendors appeared at least once. The full alphabetical table includes five vendors with zero matches. A count follows the source's recorded identity and aliases; it should not be reassigned to a related edition just because two product names share a word.

For the very-small-office question, Curve Dental appeared in all three answers and Dentrix Enterprise in none. In the multi-location dental-service-organization question, Curve Dental appeared once and Dentrix Enterprise in all three. These small cells describe the captured answers, without testing either product's suitability for those settings.

[Every figure comes from the published method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

### One retained answer

Open-source software makes its underlying source code available to inspect and modify under the applicable license. In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Claude responded to the new-practice dental software question on 22 September 2026, run 2, with the fragment “Open Dental is open-source”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Before comparing a feature, resolve the product name in the answer. Keep edition, deployment context and the cited source together. That prevents a general supplier mention from becoming an unsupported claim about the exact system your office is considering.

Use the practice context to choose which answer to read. A small office and an organization operating across locations can ask different questions of a system. The observed difference above is a prompt to inspect the wording, rather than evidence that the engine has verified either organization's requirements.

If you maintain a dental-software page, publish the facts that distinguish the actual product. When a description is wrong, preserve the claim and the source that resolves it. Adding the three Dentrix rows into one new total would blur identities and could count the same answer more than once.
